objectives: Implement stable partitioned ingestion in the prepared P5 scaffold.
Distinguish event identity from offset position.
retrieval: L101: why is an offset partition-scoped?
L102: why is changing the partition count a migration?

sections.title: The prepared artifact and the one-hour boundary
sections.markdown:
Open projects/learner/events.py and projects/P5.md. P5 uses one SQLite database to model a partitioned immutable log; it is not a replicated broker. In this first milestone implement table/config setup and ingest. Projection consumption, windowing, and production deployment are outside this hour.

Budget:10minutes read/predict,25 implementation,15 focused tests,10 evidence. Keep the accepted event's stable ID, account, payload/version, event_time, partition, and offset. The invariant is that an accepted event ID always names the same immutable payload and position.

sections.title: A transaction assigns identity and position
sections.markdown:
Hash the account deterministically with SHA-256 and reduce into the configured partition count. Do not use Python's process-randomized built-in hash for durable routing. Persist partition count and reject opening existing data with a different count. Inside a bounded write transaction, check an existing event ID; identical payload returns the previous position, conflicting payload is an error. For a new event allocate the next offset in its partition and insert it atomically.

Two concurrent writers must not both read MAX(offset)+1 and insert outside a protected transaction. A unique(partition,offset) constraint catches collisions, but the transaction/retry strategy must produce a useful result rather than silently losing the event. SQLite serializes writers in this teaching implementation; explain that boundary rather than claiming distributed consensus.

sections.title: Test your implementation, then compare the reference
sections.markdown:
Run from the repository root with Python3.11+. These are explicit terminal commands; the website does not execute submitted code.

~~~powershell
$env:ACADEMY_LAB_IMPLEMENTATION = 'learner'
py -3 -m unittest discover -s projects/tests -p test_projects.py -k P5_1 -v
Remove-Item Env:ACADEMY_LAB_IMPLEMENTATION
~~~

The default test target is the separate reference. Setting learner is necessary to evaluate your work. The supplied reference milestone check has passed; this does not mean your TODO implementation passed. Expected focused behavior: identical duplicate returns the original tuple, same-account events keep partition affinity, and offsets increase. Add a conflicting-payload assertion and reopen the database before claiming restart behavior.

sections.title: Trace a routing migration failure
sections.markdown:
Record event e1 for account a under four partitions. Predict what happens if a later process silently switches to five. The same account may now map elsewhere, its old checkpoint has a different meaning, and entity ordering across the old/new partition histories is undefined. Reject the configuration mismatch and propose a future versioned migration with a barrier instead.

Your evidence note should contain the command and real output, two event identities/positions, a duplicate replay result, and a limitation. Stop when the focused test and explanation are complete. Optional extension: model skew with one hot account and measure which partition receives it; do not label the simulated distribution a broker throughput benchmark.

diagrams.title: A durable identity and partition-local position
diagrams.source:
flowchart LR
E[Event ID plus immutable payload] --> V[Validate and stable account hash]
V --> T[Bounded SQL transaction]
T -->|New ID| A[(Append partition offset)]
T -->|Same ID same payload| R[Return original position]
T -->|Same ID changed payload| X[Reject conflict]
diagrams.caption: Single SQLite authority. The hash assigns placement; the transaction protects durable identity and offset allocation.
steps: Resolve duplicate identity in the transaction.
Append once or return the original position.

exercise.prompt: Implement P5.1 ingest in the learner scaffold and record the focused P5_1 test output, a payload-conflict case, and a restart/routing-configuration observation.
rubric: Atomic immutable event identity and offset.
Honest actual test evidence and limits.
exercise.solution: The reference uses deterministic SHA-256 routing with persisted partition count and a serialized SQL write transaction. It compares normalized event payloads for duplicate IDs and returns their existing positions, otherwise appends a unique partition/offset. Inspect projects/reference/events.py after the attempt. The passing reference proves the fixture behavior in one SQLite authority; it does not establish multi-broker replication, unbounded throughput, or your own learner implementation.

questions.prompt: Why not use Python hash(account) for durable routing?
questions.explanation: Use a deterministic algorithm and stable encoding/configuration.

questions.prompt: Same event ID with a changed amount should do what?
questions.explanation: One stable event identity cannot quietly change its meaning.

questions.prompt: What does this lab not prove?
questions.answer: Distributed replication, broker availability, production throughput, or external exactly-once effects. Its atomic boundary is one SQLite database.
questions.explanation: Distributed replication, broker availability, production throughput, or external exactly-once effects. Its atomic boundary is one SQLite database.

flashcards.back: Event ID names a logical immutable event; offset names its partition position.
A routing/history migration, not a harmless runtime toggle.
Identity, immutable payload, and unique partition-local offset together.

mentalModel: Keep logical identity stable while making physical position explicit and recoverable.
